label: End-of-input / delimiter detector, driven by how many tokens from {c,u,o,e,n,f,w,0,z} have been seen
explanation: Fires mostly at the <DEL> step (34% of delimiters active, 59% of activation mass), and also on late original-phase steps (t=4..9) where the input token is a first occurrence (39% of mass). It almost never fires in the copy phase after recall_idx 1, or at t<2. Whether it fires appears to depend on a distributed code over the prefix: it is more likely when the prefix contains tokens from {c,u,o,e,n,f,w,0,z} (by first_tok, next_out, prev/prev2). The strongest activations are at <DEL> on short sequences that start with u/c/o and contain e/f/0. Requiring at least 2 such tokens at <DEL> (or at least 3 on first-occurrence original steps) gives dev F1 about 0.49, mass recall 0.74. The token set is only an approximation of a graded, distributed dependence, so precision stays near 0.4.
